D-2 and D-3 claims to be the owner of the suit property purchased by them from D-1 on the basis of possession letter, and subsequently relied upon some electricity and water bills/connection (marked as Mark C and D) in their favour, whereas, at the same time, the plea of adverse possession is taken.

59. Suffice to state that if the possession was permissive in terms of the case so set up by the defendants, there cannot be a case of adverse possession.
60.

Be that as it may be, it is well settled that to establish the title by adverse possession, the claimant must prove the necessary requirements with clear and cogent evidence i.e. actual and open possession, hostile, continuous and to the knowledge of the true owner for the entire statutory period, and the fact that such possession continued peacefully, openly and uninterruptedly for a period of 12 years proceeding the receiving of the institution of the suit.

61. In the present case, besides making the oral statements to the effect of adverse possession, D-2 &
D-3 have failed to lead any positive evidence to show their possession was open, continuous and hostile to that of D-1 or plaintiff for that matter.
62. D-1, who was the original allotee of the plot in question, has categorically deposed that he has sold the suit property to the CS DJ No. 10145/2016 Kanti Devi vs. Rampal and Ors.

77. The possession slip Ex.D2W1/1 so produced by the D-2 in his evidence was a torn document wherein, the name of the allottee was apparently missing, and is also of no assistance to the case of the defendants.
78. The possession slip Ex. PW-1/2 produced by the plaintiff was disputed by the defendants to be forged and fabricated.
However, despite being given specific directions and opportunity to lead evidence in that regard, no witness was examined by the defendants to prove the factum of its forgery or falsity so alleged.
